name: Moped
description: A pedaled two- or three-wheeler with a seat whose motor is rated at 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or less and can't propel it faster than 30 mph; an electric bike with a motor of 750 W or more, or one outside the three e-bike classes, lands here while it stays within those limits.

restrictions.rule: Pedals for human propulsion, a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels
Its motor is rated at no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground
An automatic drive: no clutching or shifting by the rider once the drive system is engaged
Without pedals it isn't a moped, whatever its power: it's a motorized scooter if it can't exceed 20 mph, otherwise a motorcycle
Riders need a driver's license and must be 16 or older; no motorcycle endorsement, since the licensing law's motorcycle definition excludes mopeds
Riders 16 or older needn't wear a helmet or eye protection
Registered with FLHSMV, with the plate permanently affixed and visible from the rear; it isn't titled
Registering it doesn't require insurance: PIP and property damage liability proof applies only to vehicles with four or more wheels
Carries a passenger only on a seat designed for one
Not allowed on sidewalks or bicycle paths
